entries.description: Register. Journal the two decisions this set takes as authored: **derive, never write** (with options 1 and 3 recorded as the rejected alternatives), and **display-only** — the derived state changes no exit code, no `log_step` vocabulary, and nothing stored on disk. Journal the three operator rulings on the timestamp (start only, no date handling, no time on an unstarted row).

**Derive the active step in `build_rows()`.** The lowest-numbered seeded `plan-step` row with nothing logged against it, in the session `session-state.json` reports as in-progress. It must **never override what the record already says**: an explicitly logged status of any kind (including the 40 real `in-progress` writes, `blocked`, and `failed`) wins, and an *unrecognized* status token — the five legacy prose rows — is not read as evidence of anything.

**Falsify in both directions** (`L-112-1`). FIRES: an in-flight session's first unlogged planned step renders `[~]`, including retroactively on a historical set that never wrote the token. DOES NOT FIRE: a completed session marks nothing; a session whose planned steps are all logged marks nothing; a set with no seeded plan renders exactly as before; a `blocked` row is not overwritten. STRUCTURAL: at most one derived in-flight row per session, whatever the log contains.

**Confirm the projection agrees.** `session_projection` serializes what `build_rows()` returns, so assert the derived state reaches it — if it does not, there is a second implementation, which is the thing Set 120 S3 removed.
Targeted pytest for the changed modules; verify; close.

**Derive the start time onto the row.** The previous step's completion, or the session's `startedAt` for the first step; `None` for a row that has not started, so nothing downstream can render a registration timestamp as a start. Falsify the boundaries (first step, a gap between steps, an unstarted row, a session with no seeded plan).

Registered session 1 of set 127 with start_session (github-copilot / anthropic / claude-opus-5, 3 sessions). Journalled the three decisions Step 1 names: DERIVE-NEVER-WRITE (options 1 and 3 from the source-of-record note recorded as the rejected alternatives, rubric prefer-reversible), DISPLAY-ONLY (the derived state moves no exit code, adds nothing to the log_step vocabulary, and is read by no gate), and the three operator rulings on the timestamp (start only, no date handling, no time on a row that has not started) journalled verbatim as human-authority and tagged for the UAT Decide section.

In progress. session_checklist.build_rows now derives the active step: the first seeded plan row nothing has logged against, in a session session-state.json reports as in flight, and ONLY where the record is silent -- any row already boxing [~] or [!] stands the derivation down entirely, which is what stops it re-creating the two-current-rows defect the removed <- here marker produced. Eligibility asks for a token the renderer boxes [ ], so an unrecognised prose status is evidence of nothing in either direction. The raw status is never touched; ChecklistRow.effective_status is what the box is drawn from. _reconcile now returns (row, completion) pairs so the start time can be derived in the same pass. Falsifiers still to write.

Derivation landed in session_checklist.build_rows via _active_step_index + _derive_progress, plus session_flight_facts (the one read of session-state.json for both in-flight and startedAt). NOT-A-MARKER guards, each with its own falsifier: only a seeded plan row is eligible; only a session the state file reports in-flight; stands down entirely when any row already boxes [~] or [!]; eligibility requires a token the renderer boxes [ ], so an unrecognised prose status is evidence of nothing. The record is untouched -- raw status stays as written and ChecklistRow.effective_status is the display token. Existing expectations updated where they encoded the pre-derivation answer (test_plan_seeding: 6 assertions, one test renamed to test_the_step_after_the_last_logged_one_is_where_the_session_is with the reversal argued in its docstring); _in_flight now reads the box (what is shown) and record_post records the derived key because the render it attests drew it. Targeted suites green: 114 + 156 passed.
In progress. Writing the both-direction falsifiers for the derivation.

Both-direction falsifiers landed: TestTheDerivedActiveStep (FIRES retroactively on a ledger that never wrote the token, with the on-disk record asserted unchanged afterwards; DOES NOT FIRE on a closed session, an all-logged plan, a logged in-progress row, a blocked row, an unrecognised prose status on either a planned or a logged row, or a set with no seeded plan; STRUCTURAL: exactly one derived row over a six-row plan logged out of order) and TestTheDerivedStartTime (first row = session startedAt, each later row = the previous row completion including across a 35-minute gap; no time on an unstarted row, none from the plan registration stamp, none for a legacy set with no state file). PROVEN TO BITE, not merely green: four planted mutations run against the suite -- dropping the record-wins guard (3 failures), ignoring the in-flight gate (8), marking every eligible planned row (8), and reading a plan row registration stamp as a completion (initially SURVIVED, which exposed a blind spot; added the logged-row-after-an-unclaimed-plan-row case and it now fails). L-112-1 cited.
In progress.

session_projection._step_from_row now reads the row effective_status for state and box and carries isActive + startedAt, so the derived state reaches session-progress.json with no second implementation -- the projection still serializes what build_rows returns. New falsifier asserts it through write_projection/read_projection (the FILE, not the in-memory dict) plus the record-versus-display split: status stays pending, state/box say in-progress, isActive says why they differ, current and counts follow state. docs/session-progress-schema.md updated: the shape block, a new isActive/startedAt section with the derivation rules and the wall-clock-proxy caveat, the inputs table (session-state.json now also contributes startedAt), the current-is-a-list section (why this is not the <- here marker returning, point by point), and the parity section (the derived fields are proven through the file and are not yet in the cross-language corpus, with the trigger that closes that window named).
In progress.

Complete -- authored in the same pass as step 2 because both facts are one derivation over one row list, and computing them separately would be a second place for them to disagree. ChecklistRow.started_at is the previous row completion, seeded with the session startedAt for the first row; None for a row that has not started. _reconcile returns (row, completion) pairs so a seeded plan row contributes NO completion at all -- its dateTime is registration time, one stamp shared by the whole plan, and the mutation that reads it as a completion is one of the four planted in step 3. Boundaries falsified: first step, a 35-minute gap between steps, an unstarted row, a logged row whose predecessor never completed, and a set with no state file.

Targeted pytest across the nine suites touching these modules: 351 passed. Cross-provider verification, two discovery rounds, both VERIFIED on both lenses (spec-conformance and failure-scenario), 0 blocking findings in either. Round 1 returned two nits, both accepted and fixed with their own falsifiers -- the plan-less state carve-out (no sessions[] ledger, top-level startedAt) lost the first row start time, and bookkeeping records were acting as step completions in the start-time chain; the fix made the rule say what the spec says (the previous STEP completion), so a bookkeeping row is transparent while an unclaimed plan row still breaks the chain. Round 2 re-stamped clean; its one remaining nit (a non-complete logged status read as a completion) is recorded as an adjudicated-minor residual owned by Session 2. Full pytest run of record: 4055 passed, 9 skipped, 963s, recorded after the last code change. mocha and playwright owe nothing -- this session touched no surface they cover.
Register.

**Mirror the derivation in `sessionStepModel.ts`,** the model the tree actually reads, then **enumerate every consumer of a row's status** before declaring it done (`L-069-1`, and the authoring guide's echo-pass anti-pattern): `stepDescriptor`'s glyph *and* its tooltip, which currently says `planned — not started` for any planned row and would otherwise call the running step not-started in prose while showing it as running in the icon.

**Falsify in TypeScript with the same both-direction pairs, and pin the parity.** A shared fixture drives both implementations and asserts they agree row-for-row — two mirrored derivations that no test compares are two derivations that will diverge.

**Layer 3 rendering smoke**, then the human look: assert the in-progress glyph renders on the active step of an in-flight fixture session, run the full `npm run test:playwright` **after the last code change** (L-064-12), and only then offer the one-item guided walk.
Full pytest and the Layer 3 run recorded as runs of record; verify; close.

**Mirror the start time and render it `12:06-`.** Same derivation as Session 1, in the TS row model, displayed in the step row's **dimmed description slot** — `RowDescriptor.description`, which VS Code renders in grey immediately after the label, as session rows already do with `in flight`. Not concatenated into the label, which is narrow and already carries the step text plus its own label tests. That slot is currently **empty on every step row** and its own comment says why: it held the `<- here` marker until Set 115 S4 retired it. The timestamp reuses the slot that was vacated by a worse answer to the same question, so nothing is displaced. Local time, 24-hour, hour and minute only, trailing dash; the full timestamp goes in the tooltip, where width is free. A row with no derived start renders no description at all — the slot stays as empty as it is today.
Mirror the Set 127 S1 derivation (active step + start time) in sessionStepModel.ts and enumerate every consumer of a row status.

Mirrored session_flight_facts / _active_step_index / _derive_progress / effective_status in sessionStepModel.ts (reconcile now returns RowEvidence), plumbed the flight facts through SessionStepLedger + buildStepLedger, and enumerated every consumer of a row status: stepDescriptor's glyph AND its tooltip both now read effectiveStatusOf, with a step-active contextValue token.

Extended the shared parity corpus from 14 to 22 cases with the two inputs the derivation needs (per-case sessionState, per-entry dateTime) and both derived fields on every expectedRow; closed the S1 field-set split (DERIVED_ROW_FIELDS removed, isActive/startedAt now compared in both languages); both halves independently assert the corpus still pins the derivation in both directions, and both re-run every case with the state file withheld.

Start time mirrored onto the TS row model and rendered as 12:06- in the step row's dimmed description slot (stepStartLabel), with the full timestamp in the tooltip; a row with no derived start renders no description at all.

Registered session 2 of set 127 via start_session (github-copilot / claude-opus-5 / anthropic), read the preload, and posted the step checklist. The three decisions this set takes were journalled at session 1 registration and are settled; this session ratifies nothing new.

Layer 3 rendering spec updated and green (4/4): the seeded-plan scenario now asserts the derived in-progress glyph on the first unlogged planned row, exactly one such row, and the HH:MM- start time in the description slot with no time on an unstarted row; the refresh scenario asserts the derivation STANDS DOWN the moment a step is logged in-progress. Eight planted mutations across both languages were each caught by the new falsifiers. The uat-matrix fixture the walk runs on was given a seeded session-2 plan so the walk demonstrates the feature, and its rendered rows are pinned by a Layer 2 test through the real scan. s2-uat-walk.md authored (one Look item, two Decide items) and offered.
Full pytest and the full Layer 3 Playwright run, recorded as runs of record after the last code change.

Full pytest 4092 passed / 9 skipped; full Playwright 31 passed; full mocha 1520 passing -- all three recorded as runs of record, and mocha + Playwright RE-RUN and re-recorded after the round-1 remediation staled them. Verification: round 1 discovery (fan-out 2, gpt-5.5 both lenses) 1 Major; round 2 supplementary VERIFIED nothing new; remediated once with a pre/post-fix-discriminating falsifier; round 3 remediation-review VERIFIED, fix accepted, 0 findings. close_preflight: test_run_fresh green, uat_walk_recorded green, checklist_posted advisory with 4 unrecoverable windows recorded honestly.
